units.title: Differentiating a quadratic risk along a probability segment
units.classification: canonical shared library node; original mathematical supplement
units.statement: Let μ and ν be probability measures on a measurable parameter space W. Let Φ map W to a real Hilbert space H and be Bochner integrable under both laws, and let y be a fixed vector in H. Write m(ρ)=∫Φ dρ, R(ρ)=‖m(ρ)−y‖², and V(w)=2⟨m(μ)−y,Φ(w)⟩. For every 0≤t≤1, the actual positive measure ρₜ=(1−t)μ+tν is a probability, Φ is integrable under ρₜ, and its mean is the affine interpolation of the endpoint means. V is integrable under both endpoint laws. The right derivative of R(ρₜ) at zero is ∫V dν−∫V dμ. The exact remainder R(ν)−R(μ)−(∫V dν−∫V dμ) is ‖m(ν)−m(μ)‖², and is therefore nonnegative.
assumptions: W is measurable; H is a complete real inner-product normed space.
μ and ν are probabilities. Φ is genuinely Bochner integrable under each; y is any vector in H.

steps.title: Stay within probability measures
steps.text: On the closed interval the two nonnegative coefficients add to one. Scaling and adding genuine integrable functions preserves integrability under the resulting measure.
steps.lean: The exact statement and proof are available in the adjacent initially folded Lean.

steps.title: Integrate the affine segment
steps.text: Linearity of the Bochner integral identifies the actual segment mean, without replacing the measure path by an unrelated vector path.
steps.lean: The exact statement and proof are available in the adjacent initially folded Lean.

steps.title: Compute the potential pairing
steps.text: The bounded linear functional defined by the fixed residual commutes with the integral. This also proves the two scalar potential integrals exist.
steps.lean: The exact statement and proof are available in the adjacent initially folded Lean.

steps.title: Differentiate and retain the square remainder
steps.text: Apply real Hilbert-space squared-norm calculus to the affine mean. Restrict its derivative to the probability interval; expand the square to obtain the nonnegative remainder.
steps.lean: The exact statement and proof are available in the adjacent initially folded Lean.

units.title: A finite empirical segment has the actual joint-risk derivative
units.classification: canonical shared library node; original mathematical supplement
units.statement: Let P be a probability law on X×ℝ, with its actual input marginal Pₓ. Let K:W×X→ℝ be a scalar feature, and assume the actual response coordinate belongs to L²(P). Choose N>0 and two indexed parameter configurations w₀,w₁ of length N. Assume only their selected feature functions K(wₐʲ,·) belong to L²(Pₓ), for a=0,1 and every index j. Let ρ₀ and ρ₁ be their literal equally weighted Dirac empirical measures, retaining repeated indices. Define fρ(x)=∫K(w,x) dρ(w), F(ρ)=∫(fρ(x)−y)² dP(x,y), and V(w)=2∫(fρ₀(x)−y)K(w,x) dP(x,y). Every mixture (1−t)ρ₀+tρ₁ for 0≤t≤1 is a probability with integrable squared loss. V is integrable under both empirical laws, and the actual scalar risk along the mixture has right derivative ∫V dρ₁−∫V dρ₀ at zero.
assumptions: W and X are measurable, and singletons in W are measurable. P is an actual joint probability; its response coordinate is in L²(P).
N>0. Only the two selected lists of feature slices are assumed to be in L²(Pₓ); global kernel measurability, a uniform feature bound, and nonsampled feature moments are not assumed.

steps.title: Use the actual finite support
steps.text: Dirac integration turns the predictor into the indexed average. Colliding particles keep their multiplicity, and every scalar function is integrable under these finite empirical laws.
steps.lean: The exact statement and proof are available in the adjacent initially folded Lean.

steps.title: Construct genuine joint L² classes
steps.text: Pull each selected feature along the actual first-coordinate marginal. Finite sums and the supplied response class construct both endpoint means and their residual in L²(P).
steps.lean: The exact statement and proof are available in the adjacent initially folded Lean.

steps.title: Identify the finite potential pairing
steps.text: Cauchy–Schwarz gives integrability of every required sampled residual-feature product. Finite integration yields the actual potential pairing as twice the residual inner product with the mean change.
steps.lean: The exact statement and proof are available in the adjacent initially folded Lean.

steps.title: Identify the scalar mixture risk
steps.text: Linearity under the finite positive-measure mixture gives the actual predictor interpolation; its square is integrable and its integral equals the squared L² residual norm.
steps.lean: The exact statement and proof are available in the adjacent initially folded Lean.

steps.title: Take the endpoint derivative
steps.text: Differentiate this affine residual norm and restrict to the probability interval. Both finite outer potential integrals already exist.
steps.lean: The exact statement and proof are available in the adjacent initially folded Lean.

units.title: Gaussian polynomial features vary continuously in L²
units.classification: canonical shared library node; original mathematical supplement
units.statement: Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel measurable structure, γ its centered standard Gaussian law with identity covariance, and p any finite real polynomial. For every unit vector w, the actual scalar function x↦p(⟨w,x⟩) belongs to L²(γ). These membership witnesses can be chosen together so that their actual almost-everywhere equivalence classes form a continuous map from the unit sphere, with its subspace topology, into L²(γ). No feature moment, uniform bound, dominating function, or continuity assumption is supplied.
assumptions: E has finite-dimensional real inner-product and Borel structures.
p is any finite real polynomial, including zero, constant and non-even polynomials. Weights form the literal unit-norm subtype.

steps.title: Construct an integrable radial envelope
steps.text: Finite Gaussian norm moments put every radial power in L². Polynomial induction produces a nonnegative B∈L² bounding every unit-weight feature, using |⟨w,x⟩|≤‖x‖.
steps.lean: The exact statement and proof are available in the adjacent initially folded Lean.

steps.title: Use the genuine feature classes
steps.text: The actual Gaussian projection theorem supplies membership of each displayed feature. The target map takes its actual equivalence class, not an arbitrary substitute.
steps.lean: The exact statement and proof are available in the adjacent initially folded Lean.

steps.title: Apply dominated convergence to the squared distance
steps.text: Pointwise polynomial continuity and the common envelope control every squared difference. The integral is exactly the squared norm of the genuine class difference.
steps.lean: The exact statement and proof are available in the adjacent initially folded Lean.

steps.title: Recover norm continuity
steps.text: The dominated squared-distance integral tends to zero. Continuity of the square root gives convergence in the L² norm.
steps.lean: The exact statement and proof are available in the adjacent initially folded Lean.

units.title: Scalar feature averages equal their Bochner L² means
units.classification: canonical shared library node; original mathematical supplement
units.statement: Under the same finite-dimensional real inner-product, Borel and finite-polynomial assumptions, let Φ(w) be the actual L² class of x↦p(⟨w,x⟩) under the standard Gaussian γ. The feature membership witnesses are produced together with continuity of Φ. For every probability law ρ on the unit sphere, the scalar feature is genuinely integrable in w for every fixed x, and Φ is genuinely Bochner integrable under ρ. The literal scalar-average function x↦∫p(⟨w,x⟩) dρ(w) belongs to L²(γ), and its actual L² class equals ∫Φ dρ. All membership, measurability and integral-exchange obligations are conclusions of the theorem.
assumptions: E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel structure; p is any finite real polynomial.
ρ is any probability measure on the literal unit-norm subtype. No domination, moment, Bochner integrability or averaging identity is assumed.

steps.title: Build the actual radial envelope
steps.text: Gaussian norm moments and finite polynomial induction supply a common nonnegative L² envelope for all unit-weight scalar features.
steps.lean: The exact statement and proof are available in the adjacent initially folded Lean.

steps.title: Produce both forms of parameter integrability
steps.text: For fixed x the envelope is a finite constant on the parameter space. Continuity and the Gaussian ridge norm bound give Bochner integrability of the actual L² feature map under every probability law.
steps.lean: The exact statement and proof are available in the adjacent initially folded Lean.

steps.title: Construct the scalar mean class first
steps.text: Joint continuity makes the actual scalar average measurable. Its norm is bounded by B, so it belongs to L² before any class identity is used.
steps.lean: The exact statement and proof are available in the adjacent initially folded Lean.

steps.title: Justify Fubini for every L² test class
steps.text: For any genuine g∈L²(γ), Cauchy–Schwarz makes |g|B integrable. This dominates the actual product kernel, so Fubini interchanges its two genuine scalar integrals.
steps.lean: The exact statement and proof are available in the adjacent initially folded Lean.

steps.title: Identify the two Hilbert-space elements
steps.text: Each inner integral is the inner product with Φ(w). Commuting a bounded linear functional with the Bochner mean and testing against every g proves equality of the two actual classes.
steps.lean: The exact statement and proof are available in the adjacent initially folded Lean.

units.title: An actual Gaussian joint-data risk has a first variation
units.classification: canonical shared library node; original mathematical supplement
units.statement: Let P be an actual probability law on E×ℝ, where E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel structure. Assume only that its input marginal is the standard Gaussian and its actual response coordinate Y is square-integrable. Let p be any finite real polynomial. For any probability ρ on the unit sphere define fρ(x)=∫p(⟨w,x⟩) dρ(w), F(ρ)=∫(fρ(x)−y)² dP(x,y), and Vρ(w)=2∫(fρ(x)−y)p(⟨w,x⟩) dP(x,y). Every squared loss is integrable, and every displayed inner residual-feature product is integrable at every unit direction. For any two parameter probabilities ρ₀,ρ₁, Vρ₀ is integrable under both laws. The actual scalar risk along (1−t)ρ₀+tρ₁ has right derivative ∫Vρ₀ dρ₁−∫Vρ₀ dρ₀ at zero, and F(ρ₁)≥F(ρ₀)+∫Vρ₀ dρ₁−∫Vρ₀ dρ₀.
assumptions: E has finite-dimensional real inner-product and Borel structures. P is a true joint probability with standard Gaussian first marginal.
p is any finite real polynomial, and the actual second-coordinate response belongs to L²(P). Input and response need not be independent.

steps.title: Pull the actual mean to the joint data law
steps.text: The first-coordinate map preserves the actual marginal measures. Its continuous linear L² isometry commutes with Bochner integration, transporting the scalar-average class identity to L²(P).
steps.lean: The exact statement and proof are available in the adjacent initially folded Lean.

steps.title: Identify the true squared risk
steps.text: Subtract the actual label class. Its squared norm is the literal integrated squared residual. Cauchy–Schwarz also gives genuine residual-feature product integrability at every direction.
steps.lean: The exact statement and proof are available in the adjacent initially folded Lean.

steps.title: Identify the actual potential
steps.text: Almost-everywhere representative identities give the exact residual-feature inner-product formula. The bounded linear residual functional proves integrability of this scalar potential under both parameter laws.
steps.lean: The exact statement and proof are available in the adjacent initially folded Lean.

steps.title: Use the positive probability segment
steps.text: Apply the actual probability-segment mean calculus, and identify its norm risk with the literal scalar risk at every point of the interval. Restriction at zero gives the stated right derivative.
steps.lean: The exact statement and proof are available in the adjacent initially folded Lean.

steps.title: Obtain linear convexity
steps.text: The difference between the risk increment and the potential pairing is the squared mean increment. Its nonnegativity gives the supporting inequality with the correct sign and factor two.
steps.lean: The exact statement and proof are available in the adjacent initially folded Lean.
